criteria.retire_with_register: Let runners go as soon as wire legs pass, and keep every check-blocked leg in a durable coverage register inside the checklist and the Can headers: check name, missing primitive, parking date. The migration closes all 28 records with openly declared holes; the register, not running code, preserves the uncovered checks.
criteria.runners_stay: Any runner with a check-blocked leg stays permanently: .mjs/.ts files keep executing that coverage in CI or on request, while the Can files beside them own the wire legs and document the blocked ones. The goal lands at 28 minus the named parked records, which are reported as not migrated rather than retired.
criteria.substitute_narrow_property: Allow retirement only alongside a live Can verdict per leg, where the verdict may assert a tighter production truth than the original check: the server's literal CSP directive instead of the browser's block, literal set-cookie strings instead of jar conduct. Legs with no sincere narrowing keep their runners per the runners-stay rule.

blocked_retirement.instructions: Choose the rule that decides runner retirement for checks beyond any Can mechanism, keeping the 28-record closeout truthful.

state.aspect_vs_check: Keep two block strengths apart. Aspect-blocked means Can proves the property through a different shape while one facet stays unverified: caps and single-use stand proven by sequential A01/A02/B04 runs with simultaneity alone unverified, and those retirements are closed precedent. Check-blocked means Can proves nothing about the check: 'Chromium signals a CSP breach' and 'the jar rejects a forged __Host- cookie' have zero Can execution path. Only the check-blocked class is under judgment.
state.blocked_inventory: Unexecutable checks include the C03 probe.ts browser ending (lines 227-277, two groups), around five of nine proof.mjs groups, and the strict-redirect.mjs form-action denial with its click-chain cookie assertions. They require live script execution plus DOM/style/font/media readback (getComputedStyle, fonts.ready, naturalWidth, clicks), a true cookie store (__Host- handling, HttpOnly, SameSite, redirect carriage, forgery denial), in-browser CSP breach events (securitypolicyviolation), navigation with default and overridden referrers, and worker/serviceworker control. Proving service from a TLS listener is check-blocked client-side (Bun fetch fails the self-signed fixtures, demonstrated 2026-10-02); bind-only legs remain live.
state.gate_text: Standing gate: host harnesses retire only once their surviving legs pass as live Can verdicts against actual production behavior, F01 reconciles the set, and the count admits solely fulfilled obligations. Twenty-eight records cover 21 code files, 3 documents, and 4 additional owned artifacts; C02 contributes 2 .mjs runners, C03 contributes 2 .ts probes plus README.md, C04 contributes 5 fixtures. The browser-free S04 (approval_probe.ts) is expected to retire without residue.
state.mandate: AI agents write this language and owe prior artifacts nothing; reaching the goal outranks scaffolding and layered proofs by project rule. A prior unanimous Jev round (3/3, 0.96+ confidence, 2026-10-02), user-confirmed, set the course: port all wire-observable legs, mark the rest blocked, build no new runtime. This decision fixes how the blocked rest counts at the end.
state.precedent_pressure: Twelve fulfilled records set a clean bar: each retired runner left zero check-blocked legs (the extreme precedent is aspect-blocked simultaneity next to a sequentially established property). C02/C03 introduce the first fully unexecutable checks, so this ruling becomes the migration's yardstick for unportable coverage at F01.
